record cards. Repeated records and multiple cards from one context are not

claims.claim: The query is sulfisoxazole, a sulfanilamide/isoxazole; L4 records for sulfonamide-class drugs consistently show high fraction absorbed, including sulfamethizole 85% in humans (C53), sulfapyridine almost completely absorbed (C51, C61), gliclazide almost completely absorbed (C60), and glipizide FA >95% (C57).

L5 Caco-2 records show high A-B permeability (14.9-37.5 x10^-6 cm/s) with efflux ratios near unity (0.79-1.14), indicating no gut-wall efflux barrier; the sulfonamide-containing analogs C63 and C72 are directly relevant, and C62/C67 also show high permeability without efflux.

L6 human liver microsome records for the close analog sulfamethoxazole show low intrinsic clearance (0.29-0.79 µl/nmol/min; C77, C79, C81, C82), indicating limited hepatic first-pass loss; recombinant CYP2C9 values (C74, C83) are overexpression assay values and do not establish high in vivo hepatic clearance.
No supplied record provides affirmative evidence for F below 20%; the L6 hepatic-clearance evidence is mechanistically supportive rather than contradictory.

evidence_gaps: No direct absolute oral bioavailability measurement exists for the query molecule.
No matched oral versus intravenous AUC data are available for the query.
No query-specific Caco-2, intestinal metabolism, or hepatic clearance data are available; L5/L6 records use close structural analogs, mostly sulfamethoxazole.
